The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Liquid’s bitcoin IOUs are fully backed again after a $320 million exploit. A final 250 BTC transfer closed the hole left by September’s bug, but the federation behind the network still hasn’t said who paid to fill it. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Tether holds 150,000 bitcoin worth $11.5 billion, CEO Paolo Ardoino says. Ardoino didn’t say where the extra coins sit. Holdings outside USDT reserves, such as Tether’s investments, wouldn’t appear in the report. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Live news: Bitcoin faces fifth weekly loss as midterm elections weigh on markets. A fifth straight weekly decline would mark bitcoin’s joint third-longest losing streak, as oil rebounds and Apple’s margin warning adds to investor caution ahead of the U.S. midterms. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

North Korea denies role in $6.4 billion Binance hack after FBI points to TraderTraitor. The high-profile denial follows FBI alerts identifying North Korean-controlled wallet addresses tied to the largest cryptocurrency exploit in history. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Mercado Bitcoin pledges to cover all user losses after near $40 million hack. Partners like Tether, Circle, and Chainalysis helped freeze $11M of the stolen assets. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Bitcoin’s latest chart signal looks a lot like the ones before its big crashes. The Guppy Multiple Moving Average bands signal a bearish momentum, even as seasonality and post-midterm history lean bullish. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $77,140 with a -0.92% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $2,270.79 with a -0.59% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

items.title: Ethereum ETFs Outpace Bitcoin ETFs in 2026 Inflows
items.description:
Ethereum ETF inflows into U.S. spot Ethereum (CRYPTO:ETH) funds reached approximately $1.5 billion, surpassing the $985 million that spot Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) ETFs brought in. This data, sourced from SoSoValue, shows daily crypto ETF inflows and outflows. Spot ETFs directly hold the coins, so their share prices rise and fall with the cryptocurrency's market value. [...] Ethereum ETFs pulled in $1.5B in 2026 inflows, topping Bitcoin's $985M, yet Bitcoin ETFs still hold $109B in total assets, a figure roughly six times greater.
 Bitcoin ETFs staged a massive Q3 recovery, attracting $6.3 billion after $5 billion in net outflows during the first half of 2026.
 Ethereum is outpacing Bitcoin's inflow rate by $525M annually, but closing Bitcoin's $44B cumulative lead would still take over 80 years. [...] Over the years, Bitcoin ETFs have collected a staggering $57.6 billion in net inflows since their inception, whereas Ethereum funds have garnered $13.8 billion. Bitcoin ETFs began trading in January 2024—about six months before Ethereum funds, which debuted in July 2024.

At the current inflow rate, Ethereum funds are outpacing Bitcoin funds by about $525 million annually. However, it would take more than 80 years to close the existing $44 billion gap in total inflows.

items.title: 2025 Crypto Regulatory Round-Up
items.description:
What is the GENIUS Act and how does it regulate stablecoins?

The GENIUS Act is United States legislation passed in 2025 that establishes a federal regulatory framework for stablecoin issuers. It mandates strict requirements for reserve backing, audits, and financial integrity. The law also places restrictions on the domestic offering of foreign issued stablecoins, prompting a global acceleration in stablecoin policy development. [...] National regulators that have not yet developed or implemented stablecoin regulation will continue to make progress. By July 2026, U.S. federal and state regulators are required to promulgate final regulations to implement the GENIUS Act. This will include processes to license and regulate federal stablecoin issuers, and establishing criteria that foreign stablecoin issuers must meet in order to offer their stablecoins in the U.S. In Singapore, draft legislation to implement a stablecoin regime [...] Throughout the region, regulators are paying much closer attention to the systemic role of stablecoins — particularly their use in cross‑border payments, trade settlement, and inflation hedging — and are starting to define clearer requirements around issuance, reserve backing, redemption rights, and intermediary obligations, with FATF alignment and upcoming mutual evaluations serving as a common anchor for AML/CFT expectations and supervisory priorities.

items.title: Crypto Regulation in 2026: What Changed and What’s Ahead
items.description:
Regulatory trends

Stablecoin legislation

In July 2025, President Donald Trump signed the GENIUS Act legislation into law, requiring stablecoins to be backed 1-to-1 by the US dollar or other low-risk assets. The United States has also enacted the Anti-CBDC Surveillance State Act, which prohibits Federal Reserve banks from establishing or issuing a US CBDC.

SEC and CFTC crypto clarity [...] Hong Kong has introduced a dedicated stablecoin issuer licensing regime under the HKMA and FSTB. It proposes high-quality reserve-asset backing, segregation and custody requirements, independent audits, clear redemption rights, and governance standards. Algorithmic stablecoins and unbacked arrangements will face restrictions.

ETF & tokenized-asset guidelines [...] Stablecoin payment rules in the UK are still in development and have not yet come into force. The government has outlined a future framework in which stablecoins used for payments would be subject to requirements on backing, redemption, and issuer governance, with payment-system regulators gaining expanded supervisory powers over systemic arrangements. items.title: Cryptocurrency Regulation: A Guide to U.S. & Global Policies | Britannica Money
items.description:
Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it’s an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. In the United States, Congress has moved toward establishing federal oversight of stablecoins and digital asset markets. The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins, while broader market structure legislation known as the CLARITY Act advanced in Congress in 2026 but has yet to become law. [...] United Kingdom. The U.K. began regulating cryptocurrency in 2020. In October 2023, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) introduced stricter rules on crypto advertising. The Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 also expanded oversight of stablecoins. A broader regulatory framework was approved in 2026 and is scheduled to take effect in October 2027, bringing activities including crypto trading, custody, staking, and stablecoin issuance under FCA oversight. [...] ## Key Points

 U.S. cryptocurrency regulation is evolving: Federal law now governs stablecoins, while broader legislation defining oversight of digital asset markets remains unresolved.
 Governments globally have adopted widely varying approaches to digital asset regulation, from permissive frameworks to outright bans.
 U.S. oversight is divided among regulators, including the SEC and CFTC, with the IRS treating cryptocurrency as property for federal tax purposes.
